decisions.reason: Having survived its first review and fitting very closely with the firm’s integrated airport operations strategy, this product is likely to stay on the market while management continues to learn under favorable industry conditions and available organizational slack.

This module still fits the established apron and integration business, so boundedly rational management would usually retain it, though after two years a lower-profile add-on faces somewhat more scrutiny if results lag aspirations.

Because equipment monitoring supports the firm’s move toward data-driven lifecycle services and leverages installed-base complementarities, management is likely to keep it unless accumulating evidence shows a clear shortfall versus aspirations.

Its strong alignment with the firm’s safety value proposition and customer relationships with airports and navigation providers makes retention likely, with withdrawal mainly if market acceptance proves persistently weaker than expected.
